May-Thurner syndrome is a distinct diagnosis from deep vein thrombosis, though it can cause it.
Post-thrombotic syndrome is a complication of deep vein thrombosis, not the primary diagnosis in this acute presentation.
Antiphospholipid Syndrome was ruled out by negative lab tests, making it an unlikely cause of the DVT in this case.
